chunks: So bear patiently what they say, and glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and from the parts of the night, so glorify, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased.

key_terms.بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ: With the praise of your Lord

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended times for dhikr mentioned in Surah Taa-Haa?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a directive for the Prophet and the Imams to maintain spiritual composure through consistent dhikr, specifically highlighting the significance of morning and evening remembrance (Adhkar) as a shield against worldly distractions. The mention of 'ends of the day' (atraf an-nahar) is linked by scholars to the five daily prayers, emphasizing a rhythm of worship that sustains inner peace and readiness for divine pleasure.
